services.title: Power BI dashboards
services.short: Make your most important numbers easy to understand.
services.problem: Your reports contain the numbers, but the story is difficult to see. Different teams may also be working from different definitions.
services.solution: I turn reporting questions into a focused Power BI experience, with agreed metrics, a clear data model and views designed for the people using them.
deliverables: Power BI report and editable PBIX
services.scope: A focused management dashboard or a multi-page report using your agreed data sources. Sharing, licenses and refresh constraints are scoped first.

services.title: Excel cleaning & automation
services.short: Spend less effort preparing the same spreadsheet.
services.problem: Repeated exports, inconsistent formats and manual steps make a recurring report difficult to maintain.
services.solution: I map the preparation steps, standardize the inputs and build a repeatable workflow suited to your files and team.
deliverables: Repeatable Power Query or Python workflow
services.scope: One troublesome workbook, a recurring set of exports, or a reusable consolidation process. File formats and exceptions are agreed before work starts.

services.title: SQL analysis & reporting
services.short: Get consistent answers from your database.
services.problem: Business questions span multiple tables, and a one-off query is hard to turn into dependable reporting.
services.solution: I clarify the question, check table relationships and write readable SQL that makes definitions and assumptions explicit.
deliverables: Documented SQL queries or reporting views
services.scope: An analytical question set, reusable reporting queries or a reporting dataset. Access, database version and performance expectations are assessed first.

services.title: Data matching & SKU reconciliation
services.short: Find the gaps between the lists you rely on.
services.problem: Product catalogs, supplier lists and system exports disagree because identifiers, names or formats differ.
services.solution: I agree matching rules with you, normalize the inputs, and separate confident matches from exceptions that need human review.
services.scope: Reconciliation between two or more files or systems. Match confidence, acceptable ambiguity and exception handling are defined together.

services.title: BI & reporting automation
services.short: Build a reporting process you can run again.
services.problem: A useful report still depends on copying, cleaning and combining data by hand every reporting cycle.
services.solution: I connect preparation, validation and reporting in a documented flow, with clear ownership of each refresh step.
services.scope: A recurring reporting workflow or a documented ETL process. Scheduling and production operation depend on your infrastructure and access.

services.title: Python data processing
services.short: Turn complex files into analysis-ready data.
services.problem: Your data is too inconsistent or repetitive to process comfortably with manual spreadsheet steps.
services.solution: I build a focused Python workflow to transform, combine and validate files, with inputs and outputs your team can understand.
services.scope: A data transformation job, exploratory analysis, or a reusable processing script. Dataset size, formats and operating environment determine the approach.

projects.title: Hotel Booking Analysis Dashboard
projects.label: Hospitality / Business intelligence
projects.summary: A three-page view of booking patterns, guests and room preferences. Built to make a dense hotel dataset easier to explore.
projects.challenge: Booking activity contains several connected questions: when reservations arrive, which bookings cancel, who the guests are, and what rooms or meals they choose. Looking at each question in isolation makes the overall picture harder to follow.
objectives: Bring booking indicators into an executive overview.
Separate guest behavior from room and meal analysis.
Make trends and comparisons readable through focused report pages.
projects.context: Portfolio analysis of hotel booking records. The retained screenshots show booking, cancellation, average daily rate, guest, country, room and meal fields. The source dataset and its license were not published with the portfolio.
projects.approach: The visible report organizes information into an executive summary, a guest view, and a room/meal view. Cards, time-series charts, breakdowns and report filters provide different ways to examine the same booking context.
projects.architecture: Three connected reporting views: executive summary → guests → rooms and meals. The underlying PBIX and semantic model were unavailable for inspection, so a star schema and individual DAX formulas are not asserted here.
projects.implementation: The existing Power BI recording demonstrates navigating report pages and inspecting chart details. Original screenshots are retained in full, rather than replaced with illustrative client results.
projects.outcome: The published artifacts demonstrate a multi-page Power BI report and its visual organization. They do not establish live refresh, business adoption, improved forecasting or a measured commercial result.
projects.evidence: Screenshot and recording evidence. The previous source repository is unavailable; the underlying model and calculations cannot currently be reproduced from public code.
gallery: Executive summary with booking indicators and trends.
Guest view with booking status, country and guest-type breakdowns.
Room and meal view with booking breakdowns and comparisons.

projects.title: ITI Examination Management System
projects.label: Education / End-to-end data platform
projects.summary: From examination records to reporting: a training project connecting a Flask application, SQL Server and analytical views.
projects.challenge: Exams, questions, students, instructors and attendance form a connected data problem. An application needs transactional records, while analytical reporting needs a structure suited to comparing performance.
objectives: Model examination records and the relationships between users, courses and assessments.
Support student, instructor and manager workflows in Flask.
Connect the operational design to documented analytical and warehouse views.
projects.context: A training/portfolio project associated with the ITI Power BI Developer track. Dashboard counts belong to the project dataset; they are not evidence of deployment across real institutions or paying customers. Individual contribution and any collaborators should be confirmed by the author.
projects.approach: The published repository separates Flask routes and models, SQL database and warehouse scripts, and ERD/ETL documentation. It also includes a Gemini-assisted chatbot and linear-regression helper code for exploring student performance.
projects.architecture: Flask role-based interface → SQL Server operational database → documented attendance ETL → analytical warehouse/reporting views. The repository includes database and warehouse SQL; SSIS behavior is documented, but an executable .dtsx package is not published.
projects.implementation: Student, instructor and manager routes implement exam-related workflows. Database scripts describe the operational and reporting structures. The visual artifacts show executive, student, attendance and instructor views alongside application screens.
projects.outcome: Published code and diagrams demonstrate the design of an application-to-reporting project. No controlled before/after measurement supports the former 80% processing-time claim. This is a portfolio prototype, not a production-security endorsement.
projects.evidence: Public Flask and SQL source, ERD/warehouse diagrams, ETL documentation and original report screenshots. Production use would require a separate authentication and security review.

projects.title: Olympic Games SQL Analytics
projects.label: Sports / SQL exploration
projects.summary: Relating athletes, countries and Summer/Winter Games through PostgreSQL queries and a five-table source model.
projects.challenge: Questions about athletes and national performance require joining event records with demographic and country context. Table grain and relationships matter before any aggregate can be interpreted.
objectives: Explore athlete participation and medal-related questions.
Join country and athlete attributes to event records.
Practice readable aggregations, rankings and data preparation in SQL.
projects.context: The published repository contains athletes, countries, country_stats, summer_games and winter_games CSVs. This is a learning/portfolio analysis; a complete 1896–2016 coverage claim has not been verified.
projects.approach: PostgreSQL scripts create tables, load CSVs and explore joins, grouped summaries, subqueries and window functions. The actual source uses PostgreSQL, correcting the previous portfolio's SQL Server label for this project.
projects.architecture: summer_games and winter_games connect to athletes through athlete_id and countries through country_id. country_stats adds year-specific GDP and population context. This is a five-table analytical source model, not a verified constrained production schema.
projects.implementation: The source contains exploratory SQL for sport/event counts, athlete attributes, medals and country comparisons. Some statements are draft exercises and require correction or execution-order review before reuse as a complete pipeline.
projects.outcome: The published scripts and model make SQL analysis techniques inspectable. No predictive model, verified forecast or independently reproduced numerical finding is claimed.
projects.evidence: Public PostgreSQL scripts, CSV files and an original relationship diagram. Queries were inspected, not executed against an imported database during the redesign audit.
gallery: Published Olympic analysis model linking athlete, country and games data.

projects.title: Marketing Campaign Analysis
projects.label: Marketing / Exploratory analysis
projects.summary: Exploring conversion by language, channel and audience group with transparent, unique-user calculations.
projects.challenge: Campaign-level totals can hide differences in audience, language and channel. The denominator used to calculate conversion also changes how a chart should be interpreted.
objectives: Calculate conversion using unique users rather than raw event counts.
Explore personalization and A/B analysis exercises without treating them as proven causal business results.
projects.context: Portfolio/exercise analysis presented on Kaggle, with related Python exercises in the author's public repository. The full input dataset was not available in those scripts, and the anonymous Kaggle page did not expose complete notebook output for independent reproduction.
projects.approach: The published exercises group unique user counts, separate converted users, calculate conversion ratios and explore date, language, channel and age groups. Related code also examines personalization comparisons.
projects.architecture: Campaign records → unique-user grouping → converted-user numerator and audience denominator → segment comparisons and plots. This is an analysis workflow, not a deployed attribution service.
projects.implementation: Python exercises use Pandas-style grouping and Matplotlib-style charts. Original visuals are preserved. The chart's axis says percent while plotted values may be ratios; numerical labels should be clarified before quoting them.
projects.outcome: The artifacts demonstrate segmentation and conversion-analysis work. They do not verify the old 40% marketing-spend saving, clustering implementation, or the effect of reallocating a real client's budget.
projects.evidence: Original analysis images, public related Python exercises and the author's Kaggle notebook link. Units and end-to-end reproducibility require confirmation.
gallery: Original conversion-by-language chart. Percent versus ratio units require verification.
Retained notebook screenshot showing conversion calculations and chart output.

projects.title: Credit Card Fraud Detection
projects.label: Finance / Machine learning study
projects.summary: A comparative modeling study of rare-event detection, class imbalance and the trade-off between precision and recall.
projects.challenge: Fraud detection is an imbalanced classification problem. A high overall accuracy can conceal poor detection of the rare class, making evaluation and decision thresholds central to the analysis.
objectives: Explore resampling and Focal Loss for class imbalance.
Examine precision, recall and threshold-sensitive validation outputs.
projects.context: A portfolio machine-learning project using transaction-classification data. The public tree includes train/validation/test CSVs, model artifacts and validation plots. Dataset provenance, licensing and the exact run behind each published metric need author confirmation.
projects.approach: The repository includes data preparation utilities, configurable model training, Focal Loss code, neural-network and classical-model options, and evaluation helpers for confusion matrices and precision-recall curves.
projects.architecture: Split transaction data → preparation/resampling → model training → threshold analysis → validation reports. The published code describes separate split inputs, but leakage-free execution and final test performance were not independently reproduced.
projects.implementation: PyTorch and scikit-learn support the modeling study. Configurations and evaluation code expose the chosen approach, while the original comparison heatmap shows a saved validation artifact rather than a production benchmark.
projects.outcome: The project demonstrates model-comparison and imbalance-handling techniques. The README, old portfolio and chart do not provide a single reconciled metric set; no headline F1/recall score or avoided-loss estimate is claimed.
projects.evidence: Public training/evaluation source and a retained validation comparison image. Model binaries were not loaded, training was not rerun, and this is not evidence of a live financial deployment.
gallery: Original saved model comparison on validation data; metric/run attribution requires reconciliation.
